newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Coffee - Vietnam coffee crop said delayed by rains.
newsitem.headline: Coffee - Vietnam coffee crop said delayed by rains.

text.p: Torrential rains are expected to delay the drying of Vietnam's robusta coffee crop to possibly the middle of November, regional traders said on Wednesday.
Traders said the rains are pounding the state of Dak Lak in Vietnam's highlands.
"They cannot dry the coffee beans," one trader at a Singapore-based commodity house said, adding the rains had also made it difficult to transport the coffee.

Dak Lak supplies an estimated two-thirds of the 240,000-270,000 tonnes of robusta coffee beans exported by Vietnam, the world's second biggest exporter behind Indonesia. Indonesia exports about 300,000 tonnes of robusta.
Prices in London are expected by Singapore-based dealers to move up on follow-through buying after a large draw in U.S. certified stocks, reported on Tuesday.
U.S. certified stocks fell 24,391 60 kg bags in the week ending October 18 to 5,583 bags, greatly diminishing chances for a build-up in stocks next week.
"The U.S. drawdown made the market a bit more friendly," one trader said, adding supplies were tight. "Technically, the market looks good."

The January contract in London may climb to $1,430/40 a tonne after closing on Tuesday $40 higher at $1,427, traders in Singapore said. One trader estimated the January contract would rise by $10 this afternoon.
Another bullish factor is the widening gap on the most active November/January London contract spread, an indicator of nearby supply availability, another trader said.
"The focus will be on the spread which I think is going to widen again to about US$140-$150," the trader said.
The spread stood in London on Tuesday at $122.
Vietnam may benefit from the surge in prices because almost all of Indonesia's crop has already been bought, dealers said.
"Most of Indonesia's crop has already been sold. The one coming on stream is Vietnam," one dealer said.
Prices of Vietnam's grade two, 80 percent black and broken were quoted at around $1,150 a tonne FOB Saigon port, Singapore traders said.
Indonesia's grade four coffee was being priced at around $1,250/300 a tonne, the dealers said.
